title: AlphaFold-assisted study links WFS1 dysfunction to GnRH-neuron developmental defects
summary: An integrated human-genetics, structural-modeling and experimental study identified WFS1 as a candidate modifier of congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. AlphaFold 3 models supported simulations of rare WFS1 variants, including altered protein motions that were not captured by a simple benign/damaging prediction. Cell assays found impaired protein behavior and ER-stress activation; zebrafish knockdown disrupted GnRH-neuron architecture and reduced isl1a expression, with partial pharmacological rescue. These results support a developmental mechanism in model systems, not proof that WFS1 alone causes the human disorder or that a treatment benefits patients.
ai_technology: AlphaFold 3 structural modeling; PolyPhen-2 variant prediction
organization: University of Milan; IRCCS Istituto Auxologico Italiano

evidence.tested: Two rare heterozygous WFS1 variants in two families were examined using predicted structural models, replicated molecular-dynamics simulations and cell assays. Embryonic expression studies and zebrafish wfs1b knockdown/rescue experiments assessed GnRH-neuron development and ER-stress/isl1a changes.
evidence.unknown: Oligogenic inheritance and model-system results do not establish WFS1 as a sufficient human disease cause. Pharmacological rescue is partial and includes pleiotropic effects. Predicted structure/dynamics are not experimental structural confirmation; the model contribution was not isolated by ablation.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold 3 supplied monomeric and tetrameric WFS1 models for variant-specific membrane simulations and structural interpretation. PolyPhen-2 assisted variant assessment; experimental genetics and functional assays supplied the biological evidence. AI did not independently identify the gene from the exomes.

source_review.scope: Independently read source-provenanced full publisher article text including variant-modeling Methods, structural Results, cell and developmental-model findings, limitations, affiliations and dates. Figure images and supplementary data not independently reanalyzed.
